title.zh: 卷五 本紀第五 海陵王
title.raw: 卷五 本紀第五 海陵王 Volume 5 Annals 5: Prince of Hailing

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第五 本紀第五

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5

sentences.zh: 海陵王

translations.literal: Prince of Hailing
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hailing

sentences.zh: 海陵恭王昭文，字季尚，文惠太子第二子也。

translations.literal: The Reverent Prince of Hailing, Zhaowen, styled Jishang, was the second son of Crown Prince Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: The Reverent Prince of Hailing, Zhaowen, bore the style Jishang and was the second son of Crown Prince Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，封臨汝公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru with a fief of 1,500 households.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 4: he was made duke of Linru with a fief of 1,500 households.

sentences.zh: 初爲輔國將軍、濟陽太守。

translations.literal: At first he was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as general who assists the state and administrator of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉持節、督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of South Yuzhou, and Inspector of South Yuzhou, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he took the staff, supervised South Yuzhou's armies, and became inspector of South Yuzhou, keeping his rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was advanced in title to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his title was raised to general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子薨，還都。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Wenhui died, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王卽位，爲中軍將軍，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, he was made Central-Army General with troops and staff officers appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin ascended, he became central-army general with troops and a full staff.

sentences.zh: 封新安王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an with a fief of 2,000 households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prince of Xin'an with a fief of 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，爲使持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、揚州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Longchang 1, he was made Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Yang and South Xu, and Inspector of Yangzhou, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang 1: he bore the staff with full powers, commanded Yang and South Xu, and took Yangzhou, keeping his rank.

sentences.zh: 其年，鬱林王廢，尚書令西昌侯鸞議立昭文爲帝。

translations.literal: That year, when the Prince of Yulin was deposed, Director of the Masters of Writing Marquis Luan of Xichang proposed establishing Zhaowen as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after the Prince of Yulin was removed, Xiao Luan, marquis of Xichang and director of the masters of writing, urged that Zhaowen be made emperor.

sentences.zh: 八月甲辰，以新除衛尉蕭諶爲中領軍，司空王敬則進位太尉，新除車騎大將軍陳顯達爲司空，尚書左僕射王晏爲尚書令，左衛將軍王廣之爲豫州刺史，驃騎大將軍鄱陽王鏘爲司徒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: the newly appointed Commandant of the Guard Xiao Chen was made Central Army-inspector-in-Chief; Minister of Works Wang Jingze was promoted to Grand Commandant; newly appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry Chen Xianda was made Minister of Works; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was made Director; Left Guards General Wang Guangzhi was made Inspector of Yuzhou; General of Agile Cavalry Prince Chao of Poyang was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day jiachen: Xiao Chen, newly made commandant of the guard, became central army-inspector-in-chief; Wang Jingze, minister of works, was raised to grand commandant; Chen Xianda, newly made general of chariots and cavalry, became minister of works; Wang Yan, left vice director of the masters of writing, became director; Wang Guangzhi, left guards general, took Yuzhou; Xiao Chao, prince of Poyang and general of agile cavalry, became minister of education.

sentences.zh: 詔遣大使巡行風俗。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched grand envoys to tour and inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent grand envoys to tour the realm and report on local custom.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「新安國五品以上，悉與滿敘；

translations.literal: Day dingwei, an edict said: "In the state of Xin'an, all of fifth rank and above shall receive full advancement in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Day dingwei: an edict said: "In the state of Xin'an, all officials of fifth rank and above shall be advanced to the full of their grade;

sentences.zh: 自此以下，皆聽解遣。

translations.literal: from this rank downward, all may be released from service.
translations.idiomatic: from that rank down, all may be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其欲仕者，適其所樂。

translations.literal: those who wish to serve may take posts suited to their inclination."
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to serve may take whatever post suits their wish."

sentences.zh: 」以驍騎將軍河東王鉉爲南徐州刺史，西中郎將臨海王昭秀爲車騎將軍，南徐州刺史永嘉王昭粲爲荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Valiant-Cavalry General Prince Xuan of Hedong was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; West Central-Gentleman Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai was made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Inspector of South Xuzhou Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia was made Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xuan, prince of Hedong and valiant-cavalry general, took South Xuzhou; Zhaoxiu of Linhai, west central-gentleman, became general of chariots and cavalry; Zhaocan of Yongjia, inspector of South Xuzhou, took Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以輔國將軍王詡爲廣州刺史，中書郎蕭遙欣爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Day wushen: General Who Assists the State Wang Xu was made Inspector of Guangzhou; Secretariat Gentleman Xiao Yaoxin was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day wushen: Wang Xu, general who assists the state, took Guangzhou; Xiao Yaoxin, secretariat gentleman, took Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以車騎板行參軍李慶綜爲寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: Staff Clerk on the General-of-Chariots payroll Li Qingzong was made Inspector of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengxu: Li Qingzong, acting staff clerk on the chariots-and-cavalry general's roster, was made inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以安西將軍王玄邈爲中護軍，新除後軍司馬蕭誕爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinhai: Pacifying-West General Wang Xuanmiao was made Central Colonel; newly appointed Rear-Army Major Xiao Dan was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinhai: Wang Xuanmiao, pacifying-west general, became central colonel; Xiao Dan, newly made rear-army major, took Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以冠軍司馬臧靈智爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: Day renzi: Major of the General Who Establishes Might Zang Lingzhi was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day renzi: Zang Lingzhi, major to the general who establishes might, took Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，申明織成、金薄、彩花、錦繡履之禁。

translations.literal: Day yimao: the prohibitions on figured weave, gold foil, colored floral trim, and broidered shoes were reiterated.
translations.idiomatic: Day yimao: bans on figured silk, gold leaf, floral appliqué, and brocade shoes were proclaimed again.

sentences.zh: 九月癸酉，詔曰：「頃者以淮關徭戍，勤瘁於行役，故覃以榮階，薄酬厥勞。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guiyou, an edict said: "Recently, because of corvée garrison duty at the Huai passes, men have worn themselves out on forced service; therefore we spread rank and title as a slight reward for their labor.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day guiyou: an edict said: "Lately corvée at the Huai frontier has worn men out on the march; we have therefore spread honors as a modest payment for their toil.

sentences.zh: 勳狀淹留，未集王府，非所以急舍爵之典，趣報功之旨。

translations.literal: Meritorious records have lingered and not reached the princely household—this is not the way to hurry the bestowal of noble ranks or swiftly repay achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Rolls of merit still lie idle and have not reached the palace—this is no way to hurry the giving of noble rank or repay service in good time.

sentences.zh: 便可分遣使部，往彼銓用。

translations.literal: At once send envoys in groups to go there and assess and appoint rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys at once in separate parties to go there, weigh merit, and appoint rewards."

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，以前九真太守宋慈明爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: former Administrator of Jiuzhen Song Ciming was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinsi: Song Ciming, former administrator of Jiuzhen, took Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，誅新除司徒鄱陽王鏘、中軍大將軍隨郡王子隆。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.

sentences.zh: 遣平西將軍王廣之誅南兖州刺史安陸王子敬。

translations.literal: Pacifying-West General Wang Guangzhi was sent to execute Inspector of South Yanzhou Prince Zijing of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi, pacifying-west general, was sent to kill Xiao Zijing, prince of Anlu and inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是江州刺史晉安王子懋起兵，遣中護軍王玄邈討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Zimao of Jin'an, Inspector of Jiangzhou, raised troops; Central Colonel Wang Xuanmiao was sent to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an and inspector of Jiangzhou, rose in arms; Wang Xuanmiao, central colonel, was sent against him.

sentences.zh: 乙未，驃騎大將軍鸞假黃鋮，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: Day yiwei: General of Agile Cavalry Luan was given the yellow battle-axe; within and without, strict martial law was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiwei: Xiao Luan, general of agile cavalry, was granted the yellow battle-axe; court and camp were placed under strict closure.

sentences.zh: 又誅湘州刺史南平王銳、郢州刺史晉熙王銶、南豫州刺史宜都王鏗。

translations.literal: Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Chao of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Chao, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以衛將軍廬陵王子卿爲司徒，撫軍將軍桂陽王鑠爲中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: Guards General Prince Ziqing of Luling was made Minister of Education; Pacifying-Army General Prince Shuo of Guiyang was made Central-Army General with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Day dinghai: Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and guards general, became minister of education; Xiao Shuo, prince of Guiyang and pacifying-army general, became central-army general with secretariat parity equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸巳，詔曰：「周設媒官，趣及時之制，漢務輕徭，在休息之典，所以布德弘教，寬俗阜民。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guisi, an edict said: "Zhou established matchmaker officials to hasten timely marriage; Han stressed light corvée in the doctrine of rest—thus to spread virtue, enlarge teaching, ease customs, and enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day guisi: an edict said: "Zhou set matchmakers to hurry timely unions; Han prized light levies in the canon of repose—so virtue might spread, teaching widen, custom soften, and the people grow rich.

sentences.zh: 朕君制八紘，志敷九德，而習俗之風，爲弊未改，靜言多慍，無忘昏昃。

translations.literal: I rule the eight corners and aim to spread the nine virtues, yet custom's ways remain unreformed; speaking in silence I am much troubled and do not forget to toil from dusk till dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the eight directions and mean to lay out the nine virtues, yet the habits of the age are still uncured; in quiet I brood on much that grieves me and do not forget to labor from dusk to dark.

sentences.zh: 督勸婚嫁，宜嚴更申明，必使禽幣以時，摽梅息怨。

translations.literal: Overseeing and urging marriage should be strictly reiterated, so that betrothal gifts come in season and complaints of late marriage cease.
translations.idiomatic: Oversight and urging of marriage should be proclaimed again in strict terms, so that bride-price comes on time and the sighs of waiting maidens fall silent.

sentences.zh: 正廚諸役，舊出州郡，徵吏民以應其數，公獲二旬，私累數朔。

translations.literal: Regular kitchen corvées of old came from prefectures; officials and commoners were levied to fill the quota—the public domain got two ten-day periods, private households suffered for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen corvées for the main kitchens once fell on the provinces; clerks and commoners were pressed to fill the count—the public coffers gained twenty days' labor while private homes bore the burden for months.

sentences.zh: 又廣陵年常遞出千人以助淮戍，勞擾爲煩，抑亦苞苴是育。

translations.literal: Also, every year Guanglin sent out a thousand men to aid Huai garrison service—a burden of toil and trouble, and also a nursery for gift bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Each year as well Guanglin forwarded a thousand men to the Huai garrisons—a wearisome levy, and one that bred wrapped gifts and graft.

sentences.zh: 今竝可長停，別量所出。

translations.literal: Now all may be permanently halted; other measures for levies shall be weighed.
translations.idiomatic: Let all these be stopped for good, and other sources of supply be reckoned instead.

sentences.zh: 諸縣使村長路都防城直縣，爲劇尤深，亦宜禁斷。

translations.literal: In all counties, having village heads, road wardens, and city-defense duty go direct to the county—the hardship is especially severe—and this too should be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: In every county, when village heads, road wardens, and wall-guard duty are billed straight to the magistrate, the harm is worst of all—that too must be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」丁酉，解嚴。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingyou: the strict closure was lifted.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史宣城公鸞爲太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，加殊禮，進爵爲王。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou Duke Luan of Xuancheng was advanced to Grand Tutor, bearing the title of Great General and Governor of Yangzhou, with extraordinary honors, and advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan, duke of Xuancheng, general of agile cavalry and inspector of Yang, was raised to grand tutor, great general, and governor of Yangzhou, given extraordinary honors, and advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，誅新除中軍將軍桂陽王鑠、撫軍將軍衡陽王鈞、侍中秘書監江夏王鋒、鎮軍將軍建安王子真、左將軍巴陵王子倫。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: the newly appointed Central-Army General Prince Shuo of Guiyang, Pacifying-Army General Prince Jun of Hengyang, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Library Prince Feng of Jiangxia, Suppressing-Army General Prince Zizhen of Jian'an, and Left General Prince Zilun of Baling were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuxu: Xiao Shuo of Guiyang, newly made central-army general; Xiao Jun of Hengyang, pacifying-army general; Xiao Feng of Jiangxia, attendant-in-ordinary and director of the palace library; Xiao Zizhen of Jian'an, suppressing-army general; and Xiao Zilun of Baling, left general—all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以寧朔將軍蕭遙欣爲豫州刺史，新除黃門郎蕭遙昌爲郢州刺史，輔國將軍蕭誕爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Pacifying-the-North General Xiao Yaoxin was made Inspector of Yuzhou; newly appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xiao Yaochang was made Inspector of Yingzhou; General Who Assists the State Xiao Dan was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Xiao Yaoxin, pacifying-the-north general, took Yuzhou; Xiao Yaochang, newly made gentleman of the yellow gate, took Ying; Xiao Dan, general who assists the state, took Si.

sentences.zh: 宣城王輔政，帝起居皆諮而後行。

translations.literal: As Xuancheng Prince held the regency, the emperor consulted him on all daily matters before acting.
translations.idiomatic: With the Xuancheng prince directing the government, the emperor asked his leave on every move of daily life.

sentences.zh: 思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。

translations.literal: When he wished to eat steamed fish and greens, the Director of the Palace Kitchen replied that without the regent's recorded order none could be given—and in the end he was not served.
translations.idiomatic: Craving steamed fish and vegetables, he was told by the palace kitchen director that without the regent's written command nothing could be served—and in the end he got none.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令曰：「司空、後將軍、丹陽尹、右僕射、中領軍、八座：夫明晦迭來，屯平代有，上靈所以眷命，億兆所以歸懷。

translations.literal: Day xinhai, the empress dowager's order said: "To the Minister of Works, Rear General, Administrator of Danyang, Right Vice Director, Central Army-inspector-in-Chief, and the Eight Seats: brightness and dimness alternate in turn; adversity and ease replace each other in their generations—that is why the High Spirit grants the mandate and the myriad people turn their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinhai: the empress dowager ordered: "To the minister of works, the rear general, the administrator of Danyang, the right vice director, the central army-inspector-in-chief, and the eight seats: light and shadow take turns; hardship and peace succeed one another in their seasons—thus the high spirits bestow the mandate and the myriad folk set their hearts.

sentences.zh: 自皇家淳耀，列聖繼軌，諸侯官方，百神受職。

translations.literal: Since the imperial house's pure splendor, successive sages have continued the track; feudal lords have held their posts and the hundred spirits received their charges.
translations.idiomatic: From the house's clear radiance, sage after sage has kept the path; feudal lords have held their offices and the hundred spirits their posts.

sentences.zh: 而殷憂時啓，多難薦臻，隆昌失德，特紊人鬼，非徒四海解體，乃亦九鼎將移。

translations.literal: Yet times of deep grief have opened and many calamities have piled up; Longchang lost its virtue and especially tangled the bond of human and ghost—not only did the four seas come apart, but even the nine cauldrons were about to shift.
translations.idiomatic: Yet seasons of deep sorrow have opened and many trials have gathered; Longchang lost its virtue and especially tangled the rites of the living and the dead—not only did the four seas fall apart, but even the nine cauldrons were near to shifting.

sentences.zh: 賴天縱英輔，大匡社稷，崩基重造，墜典再興。

translations.literal: By Heaven's gift of an heroic helper the altars were greatly righted; the toppled foundation was remade and fallen rites revived.
translations.idiomatic: By Heaven's gift of a heroic minister the altars were greatly set right; the fallen base was rebuilt and broken rites raised again.

sentences.zh: 嗣主幼沖，庶政多昧，且早嬰尪疾，弗克負荷，所以宗正內侮，戚藩外叛，覘天視地，人各有心。

translations.literal: The successor lord is young and tender, and most state affairs are unclear; moreover he has long borne wasting illness and cannot bear the burden—hence the house is insulted from within, kinsmen rebel abroad, and every man looks to Heaven and earth with his own heart.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning lord is young and weak, and much of government is dim to him; moreover he has long been wasted by illness and cannot bear the weight—so the lineage is mocked within, kinsmen rise without, and each man watches Heaven and earth with a separate heart.

sentences.zh: 雖三祖之德在民，而七廟之危行及。

translations.literal: Though the virtue of the three ancestors remains with the people, the danger to the seven temples is already near.
translations.idiomatic: Though the three ancestors' virtue still lives in the people, peril to the seven temples is already at hand.

sentences.zh: 自非樹以長君，鎮以淵器，未允天人之望，寧息奸宄之謀！

translations.literal: Unless a mature ruler is set up and steadied by a deep vessel, Heaven and men's hopes will not be satisfied, nor can conspiracies of traitors be stilled!
translations.idiomatic: Unless a long-established lord is raised and steadied by a deep measure, Heaven and men will not be content, nor will traitors' plots be stilled!

sentences.zh: 太傅宣城王胤體宣皇，鐘慈太祖，識冠生民，功高造物，符表夙著，謳頌有在，宜入承寶命，式寧宗祏。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Xuancheng Prince inherits the body of the Proclamation Emperor, was cherished by the Grand Progenitor from the start; his discernment crowns all living men and his merit towers above creation; signs and portents were long evident and song-praise is already there—he should enter to receive the precious mandate and thereby pacify the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xuancheng Prince carries the Proclamation Emperor's line, was beloved of the Grand Progenitor from the first; his wisdom outtops all born men and his merit rises above the made world; omens were long plain and songs of praise already ring—let him enter to take the precious mandate and settle the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝可降封海陵王，吾當歸老別館。

translations.literal: The emperor may be demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing; I shall retire in old age to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor may be lowered to prince of Hailing; I shall retire in age to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 昔宣帝中興漢室，簡文重延晉祀，庶我鴻基，於茲永固。

translations.literal: Long ago Emperor Xuan of Han revived the Han house; Emperor Jianwen of Jin prolonged Jin's sacrifice—may our great foundation here be forever firm.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Xuan of Han revived the Han house; Emperor Jianwen of Jin renewed Jin's rites—may our great foundation here stand firm forever.

sentences.zh: 言念家國，感慶載懷。」

translations.literal: Speaking with thought of family and state, gratitude and joy fill the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of house and realm, gratitude and joy fill the breast."

sentences.zh: 建武元年，詔「海陵王依漢東海王彊故事，給虎賁、旄頭、畫輪車，設鐘虡宮縣，供奉所須，每存隆厚。

translations.literal: Jianwu 1, an edict said: "The Prince of Hailing, following the precedent of the Han Prince Qiang of Donghai, shall be given Tiger Guards, feathered headgear, painted-wheel carriages, and bell and bell-stand palace music set out; whatever supplies are needed shall always be kept in generous abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 1: an edict said: "The prince of Hailing, following the Han precedent of Prince Qiang of Donghai, shall receive tiger guards, plumed headgear, painted-wheel carriages, and full palace bells and stands; whatever he needs for maintenance shall be kept in generous measure.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，稱王有疾，數遣御師占視，乃殞之。

translations.literal: " Eleventh month: he was said to be ill; imperial physicians were repeatedly sent to examine him—and then he was caused to die.
translations.idiomatic: " Eleventh month: he was reported ill; court physicians were sent again and again to examine him—and then he was killed.

sentences.zh: 給溫明秘器，衣一襲，斂以𧘠冕之服。

translations.literal: Warm-bright secret coffin furnishings were granted, one set of garments, and he was enshrouded in robes of the 𧘠-and-mian type.
translations.idiomatic: He was given warm-bright secret coffin gear, one suit of clothes, and enshrouded in xuan-and-mian regalia.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The grand herald supervised the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 葬給轀輬車，九旒大輅，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆鼓吹，輓歌二部，依東海王故事。

translations.literal: For burial he was given a wheel-hearse, the nine-tassel great chariot, yellow canopy and left great banner, front and rear feather-canopy processional bands, and two sections of dirge singers—all following the Donghai Prince precedent.
translations.idiomatic: For burial he received a wheel-hearse, the nine-tassel great carriage, yellow canopy and left great banner, front and rear feather-canopy bands, and two choirs of dirge singers—all as for the Donghai prince.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Reverent Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was canonically titled Reverent Prince.

sentences.zh: 年十五。

translations.literal: He was fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：郭璞稱永昌之名，有二日之象，而隆昌之號亦同焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Guo Pu said the name Yongchang has the image of two suns—and the era name Longchang is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Guo Pu held that the name Yongchang bears the sign of two suns—and the era name Longchang is likewise.

sentences.zh: 案漢中平六年，獻帝卽位，便改元爲光熹，張讓、段珪誅後，改元爲昭寧，董卓輔政，改元爲永漢，一歲四號也。

translations.literal: It is recorded that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian took the throne he at once changed the era to Guangxi; after the execution of Zhang Rang and Duan Gui it was changed to Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo held the government it was changed to Yonghan—four era names in one year.
translations.idiomatic: It is on record that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian ascended, the era was at once changed to Guangxi; after Zhang Rang and Duan Gui were killed it became Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo seized power it became Yonghan—four era names in one year.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，長沙王乂事敗，成都王穎改元爲永安；

translations.literal: In Jin Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha's affair failed, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha fell, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;

sentences.zh: 穎自鄴奪，河間王顒復改元爲永興，一歲三號也。

translations.literal: when Ying seized power from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian again changed the era to Yongxing—three era names in one year.
translations.idiomatic: when Ying seized rule from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian changed the era again to Yongxing—three era names in one year.

sentences.zh: 隆昌、延興、建武，亦三改年號。

translations.literal: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu also saw three era changes.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu likewise saw three changes of era name.

sentences.zh: 故知喪亂之軌迹，雖千載而必同矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the track of turmoil and ruin, though a thousand years apart, is sure to be the same.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that the path of chaos and collapse, though a thousand years lie between, is always the same.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：穆穆海陵，因亡代興。

translations.literal: In praise: Solemn, so solemn was Prince of Hailing—through the perished he rose on another's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Grave and still was the prince of Hailing—through ruin another was raised.

sentences.zh: 不先不後，遭命是膺。

translations.literal: Neither before nor after—he met the mandate as it came.
translations.idiomatic: Neither first nor last—he took the charge fate handed him.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua shuju edition of the 《Book of Southern Qi》, January 1972.
